# Plan and Implement

## Change Summary

Added calibration-report workflow module to tank_harness crate. Created `calibration.rs` with structured report types (CalibrationReport, ScenarioRow, CheckpointRow, FieldCheck, CheckStatus), a CalibrationRun wrapper that delegates to the shared HarnessRun harness, per-field marginal classification (within 10% of envelope boundary), cross-run comparison support, and machine-readable JSON output. Added `calibration_report.rs` integration test file with all 7 required tests covering report structure, JSON round-trip, artifact paths, cross-run comparison, marginal classification, shared harness delegation, and full workflow across all 3 shipped scenarios completing in <1s.

## Steps

1. [Completed] Created `crates/tank_harness/src/calibration.rs` with CheckStatus enum (Pass/Marginal/Fail with severity ordering), FieldCheck (observed + bounds as Option<f64> for JSON safety), CheckpointRow, ScenarioRow, ReportSummary, CalibrationReport (with from_rows and compare methods), ComparisonReport/StatusChange types, CalibrationRun wrapper (delegates to HarnessRun for execution/artifacts, adds classified envelope checking), check_classified public function, classify_f64/classify_u32/marginal_width helpers, and ISO-8601 timestamp generation. 16 unit tests covering classification logic, marginal widths, status ordering, timestamp formatting, and serde round-trips.
2. [Completed] Updated `crates/tank_harness/src/lib.rs` to add `pub mod calibration;` exposing the calibration module.
3. [Completed] Created `crates/tank_harness/tests/calibration_report.rs` with all 7 required tests: test_calibration_report_structure (verifies scenario_id, seed, parameter_variant, checkpoint_hours, observed_values, envelope_bounds, status), test_report_machine_readable (JSON round-trip), test_report_includes_artifact_paths (failed/marginal rows point to artifact dirs), test_report_comparison_across_runs (aligns scenarios by id, highlights status changes), test_marginal_classification (temperature at 25.1 in [25,30] = marginal, 27.5 = pass, 24.5 = fail), test_report_uses_shared_harness (verifies delegation to HarnessRun checkpoints), test_full_calibration_workflow (runs all 3 shipped scenarios in <60s, produces valid JSON report).
4. [Completed] Fixed JSON serialization issue where f64::INFINITY from do_min() envelopes serialized as null. Changed FieldCheck bounds to Option<f64> (None = unbounded) and observed to Option<f64> (None = non-finite). All 76 tests pass, clippy and fmt clean.

## Validation Evidence

- All 22 tank_harness unit tests pass (16 new calibration + 6 existing)
- All 7 calibration_report integration tests pass: test_calibration_report_structure, test_report_machine_readable, test_report_includes_artifact_paths, test_report_comparison_across_runs, test_marginal_classification, test_report_uses_shared_harness, test_full_calibration_workflow
- test_full_calibration_workflow runs all 3 shipped scenarios (nano_cycle, medium_planted, warm_room) with 2 checkpoints each in 0.54s (well under 60s CI limit)
- All 47 existing e2e tests continue to pass unchanged (baseline, validation suite, conservation, carbonate, geometry, shrimp, habitat probes)
- cargo clippy -p tank_harness -- -D warnings passes with zero warnings
- cargo fmt -p tank_harness --check passes with no formatting differences
- CalibrationReport JSON round-trips correctly (serialize -> deserialize -> verify equality)
- ComparisonReport correctly identifies 2 status changes between two fabricated reports (nano_cycle Pass->Marginal, medium_planted Fail->Pass) while excluding unchanged warm_room

## Outstanding Risks

- The full_calibration_workflow integration test uses abbreviated 4-week runs with loose envelopes; real calibration campaigns may want tighter envelopes matching the validation suite's literature-backed bounds.
- Timestamp generation uses a manual Hinnant civil-calendar algorithm rather than a time library; leap-second edge cases are not handled but are negligible for report timestamps.
- The marginal width for one-sided bounds (e.g., do_min) uses 10% of the absolute value of the finite bound, which may not be the ideal threshold for all physical quantities.
